chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The man should not wear silk and brocade except during the battle.

key_terms.الدِّيبَاج: Brocade (silk fabric with woven gold/silver threads)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on men wearing silk and brocade?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the prohibition of silk and brocade for men, a ruling rooted in the distinction between luxury and utility, while explicitly permitting its use in warfare for protection or status. In Shia jurisprudence, this exception highlights the pragmatic adaptation of dress codes to functional needs, distinguishing the battlefield context from daily social conduct. The narration underscores the principle that material exclusivity is permissible when it serves a specific, justified purpose rather than mere ostentation.
